title.narrative: ROAS/KSA/05/MoMRAH (Support to The Spatial Planning Reform and Visual Appeal Program in Saudi Arabia)

description.narrative:
Background
Vision 2030
The Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing (MoMRAH) in Saudi Arabia has been given, among others, the mandate to support the Kingdom in achieving the Sustainable Development Goals, increasing the quality of life in cities, and help implementing Saudi Vision 2030. MoMRAH is currently formalizing its contribution to Vision 2030 and aligning its programmatic efforts to the goals of the Vision, through several strategic programs. As the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia seeks to develop its own, unique approach to the development of its cities and places, MoMRAH mandate and scope of work on improving urban planning and design efforts across the country, upholds new values and acquires new meanings. The vision is in line with the United Nations principles and is a source for sustainable urban development. The NUA is a blueprint for achieving both, the SDGs as well as the aim of “increasing the quality of life in cities”. You could emphasise this fact and reference the NUA as a source for sustainable urban development. Therefore, the NUA, along with the Vision 2030 may be an additional source and for the aim of the Kingdom to transform its cities.
The MoMRAH Urban Transformation Program
In order to enforce its mandate MoMRAH has devised a complete strategy, and a specific program to be managed by the Deputyship pf Town Planning. As such, 22 initiatives, labelled around the two strategic streams of Visual Appeal and Spatial Planning, are being designed and soon to be launched and developed under the umbrella of the ‘Urban Transformation Program’. The mission of the program is to facilitate the transformation of Saudi cities, municipalities and villages in beautiful, lively and prosperous places for life, enhancing citizen satisfaction with the public realm, promoting and providing high quality urban design, wellbeing and healthy lifestyles across Saudi Arabia. Among the many initiatives constituting the program, MoMRAH has requested the support of UN-Habitat and UNDP in developing 6 of them (UN-Habitat 3 and UNDP 3).
Achieving the Urban Transformation program is central for UN Habitat in KSA strategy, as it i provides an operational opportunity to device alternative urban visions for Saudi cities in the 21st century by improving resilience, climate-proof planning as well as sustainable neighbourhood design .
The Future Saudi Cities Program (FSCP)
UN-Habitat has a long history and strong track record supporting the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia and in particular the Ministry of Municipal, Rural Affairs and Housing.
The FSCP (UN-Habitat 2015-2020) is a testimony to the long and active presence of UN-Habitat in the country and its commitment to supporting the Saudi government in implementing Vision 2030. Two years after the official closure of the FSCP program, all the major governmental agencies as well as other international organizations (ie. World Bank) continue to refer to and actively utilize the knowledge produced under the umbrella of the FSCP – in terms of facts (evidence-based assessment of Saudi urbanization trajectory), methods and results.
With the tremendous changes that took place in Saudi Arabia since 2017, the program has gained traction, while the country has become more of a fertile ground for maximizing the project outcomes, including the specific knowledge developed. Through the State of Saudi Cities, the 17 City profiles and CPI reports, decision-makers in different cities now have access to better knowledge and an improved understanding of the various urbanization issues in Saudi Arabia. They also have a suitable roadmap for making Saudi cities more livable and sustainable. In addition, the FSCP established the basis for this new project by highlighting which main issues are affecting Saudi Cities and what structural reforms need to be put in place to correct the course of action and drive urbanization towards more sustainable outcomes. As a result, the three main outcomes of this project reflect those specific needs and propose a means of addressing them in support of the Kingdom’s transformation as envisioned by Vision 2030.
National Spatial Strategy
Following the FSCP project, UN-Habitat jointly with UNDP supported a two-year project titled ‘Support for National Spatial Strategy 2030 in Saudi Arabia’. The project was designed to boost the capacity of the Government to achieve the objectives of the National Spatial Strategy (NSS) along with their alignment with the Vision 2030. The project involved providing support to the NSS Implementation Office established inside the Deputyship of Town Planning. Key outcomes included: 1) Improving capacity for the implementation of the National Spatial Strategy (NSS) 2030; 2) Improving access to urban data between line ministries in NSS 2030 platform; and 3) Improving localizing sustainable urban development at national, regional and local authorities.
